## Results

## Limits of Detection and Quantification

The LOD of the ASR was 2.25 copieslmL (180 copies/mL) Table I, which was equivalent to 1.30 copieslmL (20 copieslmL) using the Namalwa cell line. The LOQ based on an SD of 0.15 copieslmL or less was 3.90 copieslmL (Table 1). Ofnote, the SDs at 3.53 copieslmL and 2.89 copieslmL were 0.18 and 0.17 copieslmL, respectively . logio logio logio

## Linearity and Reproducibility

The assay was linear from 2.17 to 6.21 copieslmL Reproducibility was assessed by testing 7 replicates of low and high viral load patient samples and 6 replicates of the QSs. The low patient sample had a mean (SD, CV) value of 3.70 copieslmL (0.07, 2.0%). The high patient sample had a mean (SD, CV) value of 5.40 copieslmL (0.07, 1.4%) The QSs had mean Ct (SD, CV) values as follows: QSI,21.8 (0.4, 1.6%); QS2, 25.1 (0.4, 1.5%); QS3,28.5 (0.2, 0.8%); and QS4, 31.8 (0.3, 1.0%) logio logio

## Agreement

Of the 61  patient   samples   tested by the   laboratory developed method and the ASR, 35 were positive in both assays. Of the 6 samples that were positive in the Artus assay but not in the laboratory-developed assay, the average copy number was 1.62 copieslmL, with a range of 1.41 to 2.13 copieslmL. There was only sample that was positive in the laboratory-developed assay but negative in the Artus assay, with a value of 3.23 copieslmL The remaining 19 samples were negative by both assays.
